design.affected_system: public-sector analytical, scoring, triage, optimization, and human-review systems
alternatives: activate a bounded reserve from forecast risk bands for algorithmic decision review, appeal, and audit demand
use rolling forecasts and conservative capacity triggers for algorithmic decision review, appeal, and audit demand
pair decision-volume, drift, incident, recourse, and policy-change forecasting with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Model output, recommendation, human decision, action, appeal, service, and outcome remain distinct.
High-impact decisions require lawful authority, human responsibility, contestability, and incident response.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: continue ordinary capacity planning for algorithmic decision review, appeal, and audit demand.

constraints.description: The algorithmic decision support and governance forecast must respect declared validated operational capacity and forecast uncertainty.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: algorithmic accountability officer and responsible technology review board
design.decision_question: What decision, override, appeal, incident, drift, and audit workload should governance capacity prepare for?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The algorithmic decision support and governance forecast must respect declared validated operational capacity and forecast uncertainty.
independence_key.decision_object: algorithmic decision review, appeal, and audit demand
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for algorithmic decision review, appeal, and audit demand passes documented checks for held-out error, interval coverage, event detection, drift, and baseline comparison.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: decision-volume, drift, incident, recourse, and policy-change forecasting
independence_key.primary_outcome: high-impact decisions above qualified review capacity

design.intended_claim: A versioned forecast design for comparing declared alternatives affecting algorithmic decision review, appeal, and audit demand, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: high-impact decisions above qualified review capacity
distributional gap in high-impact decisions above qualified review capacity
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call forecast reviews errors, violations, harms, discrimination, or appeals filed.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for algorithmic decision review, appeal, and audit demand passes documented checks for held-out error, interval coverage, event detection, drift, and baseline comparison.

design.title: Forecast human review, recourse, and audit demand
transportability_risks: Law, institutional process, data-generating systems, populations, incentives, and recourse differ.
Technical fairness metrics may conflict and cannot establish legal or substantive fairness alone.

family.affected_system: public-sector analytical, scoring, triage, optimization, and human-review systems
claim_boundary: Area and administrative differences do not establish discrimination, preferences, or individual behavior.
Behavioral and allocation designs require rights, accessibility, privacy, and non-coercion review.
Causal, fairness, adoption, and welfare claims require direct outcomes and independent governance evidence.
family.decision_owner: algorithmic accountability officer and responsible technology review board
family.description: Eight decisions for system diagnosis, workload forecasting, control portfolios, review siting, oversight allocation, audit scheduling, failure stress, and causal system evaluation.
family.title: Algorithmic decision support and governance

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
